subject: Throughput Targeting & Mixed-GPU Fit — CondorCloud RFP Questionnaire
messages:
From: Priya Menon <pm@condorcloud.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@condorcloud.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput questionnaire for Dedicated pool (CondorCloud RFP)

Evelyn —

Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is our throughput + workload questionnaire (CondorCloud_Throughput_RFP_v1.xlsx). High level context: we are evaluating a committed Dedicated pool to replace our current mixed cluster; primary workloads are:
- Live chat (multi-turn, 2–6 prompts/session, want p95 generation latency <= 200ms for up to 8k concurrent sessions)
- Large-batch embeddings (offline, nightly jobs: 200k documents/day)
- Re-ranking pipelines (short context, high QPS)

Two areas we care about for the questionnaire: GPU family fit for each workload (H100 vs A100-80GB vs L4-like accelerators) and realistic sustained vs peak throughput assumptions for reservation planning. We also need a short note on fallbacks (if dedicated capacity saturates, what happens) and whether prefix/KV caching can be applied across sessions.

Can you return the filled sheet and a short summary of your recommended GPU mix and expected throughput numbers by EOD Monday PST? If you prefer, we can take a 30-minute intake call — procurement is looped on this thread for contracting questions.

Attachments: CondorCloud_Throughput_RFP_v1.xlsx

Thanks,
Priya Menon
Senior Product Ops, CondorCloud
pm@condorcloud.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Menon <pm@condorcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput questionnaire for Dedicated pool (CondorCloud RFP)

Priya —

Thanks for the questionnaire. We completed the worksheet (attached) and added a short throughput profile CSV that maps your three primary workloads to recommended GPU families and a conservative throughput plan for a 12-month reservation horizon. Highlights up front:

- Proposed GPU mix (initial commit):
  * Chat / low-latency, multi-turn generation: A100-80GB (int8 quant) — best latency/cost balance for 4–8k concurrent sessions with KV caching enabled.
  * Re-ranking / high-QPS short-context: mixture of H100-backed instances for peak throughput and A100s for steady-state (H100 gives better kernel throughput on very wide models).
  * Bulk embeddings: L4-class accelerators (or equivalent cost-optimized GPUs) for batch embedding runs — cheaper per-inference and good for nightly throughput.

- Throughput summary (sustained -> burst capacity):
  * Sustained baseline tokens/sec (all workloads combined): 20k tokens/sec
  * Target peak burst tokens/sec (for short windows up to 30 min): 120k tokens/sec — achieved via configured burst pool + autoscaling policy on Dedicated.
  * Expected p95 gen latency (chat workload, A100 quant path): ~140–220ms depending on sequence length and KV cache hit rate. With aggressive prefix caching we project p95 closer to 140–160ms for typical chat patterns.

Notes on caching & fallbacks:
- KV/Prefix caching: Supported and recommended for multi-turn sessions — caching reduces both compute and memory pressure; we included conservative cache-hit assumptions in the CSV.
- Fallbacks: Our routing policies let you set a prioritized fallback order. If the Dedicated pool is saturated, requests can automatically route to a compatible hosted variant or a lower-precision model. Fallbacks may increase tail latency and change token-level cost; we called this out in the attached SLO matrix.

We attached: redwood_completed_throughput_sheet.xlsx and throughput_profile.csv. We can run a 30-minute workshop to validate the assumptions; suggested times: Mon 7/20 10am PT or Tue 7/21 2pm PT.

If you prefer, I can loop in our Pricing lead (Marissa) to include committed pricing stubs.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwood.ai

From: Priya Menon <pm@condorcloud.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@condorcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput questionnaire for Dedicated pool (CondorCloud RFP)

Evelyn —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the worksheet. A couple of clarifications after scanning the CSV:

1) Can you call out the assumed model families and tokenization size used to derive tokens/sec numbers (we run a mix of 8k and 32k-context models)?
2) For KV cache behavior — is the cache per-GPU, per-pool, or shared across nodes in the Dedicated pool? What hit-rate assumptions did you use for the 140–160ms p95 estimate?
3) If we opt for an explicit committed baseline (e.g., 200-stream-equivalent), what should we expect to be the delta to on-demand price for burst capacity? Procurement wants a simple committed vs burst pricing stub to feed to finance.

We can take the workshop tomorrow 7/21 at 2pm PT (works for engineering and procurement). Please include Marissa for pricing.

Thanks,
Priya

Subject: Re: Throughput questionnaire for Dedicated pool (CondorCloud RFP)

Hi Priya —

Thanks — hopping on the 7/21 workshop is perfect. Quick answers to your numbered points to prep the call:

1) Model/context assumptions:
   - For chat: we modeled two classes — medium context (8k tokens) and long context (32k tokens). Tokenization assumed ~4 chars/token average; model families used were Redwood-Open-Chat-16k (1.3B emulation profile) and Redwood-Long-Seq-32k (estimate for your large-context runs). The CSV has per-model per-context rows.

2) KV cache topology & hit rate assumptions:
   - Cache scope: per-pool, sharded across Serving nodes with an LRU eviction policy. Dedicated pool config supports sticky-session affinity to improve cache locality for multi-turn sessions.
   - Charted assumptions: optimistic hit rate 70% (tight dialogue patterns), conservative 35% (volatile user flows). The p95 numbers in our summary used conservative 50% hit-rate.

3) Pricing delta (committed vs burst):
   - Attached is a short pricing stub (dedicated_pricing_stubs.pdf) and an SLO matrix (slo-matrix.csv). High-level: committed baseline reduces per-token/instance effective cost by ~22–30% relative to on-demand, depending on GPU mix and commitment term. Bursts beyond committed capacity are billed at an overage tier (we priced a 2.2x factor over committed unit cost for short windows). Exact delta depends on the final GPU blend — we'll finalize numbers on the call.

Attached: dedicated_pricing_stubs.pdf, slo-matrix.csv.

Proposed workshop agenda (30m):
- 0–10m: validate workload profiles & model contexts (Evelyn)
- 10–20m: discuss GPU mix options and burst model (Connor)
- 20–30m: pricing stub walk-through and next procurement steps (Marissa)

See you at 2pm PT. If anything else you want us to prep (e.g., sample SLO wording for fallbacks), reply here and we’ll add it.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing & Commercials | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
